أَبْخَعُ [More, and most, effectual to kill, and destroy]. (K voce أَخْنَعُ, q. v.) ―
-b2- هُمْ أَبْخَعُ طَاعَةً (tropical:) They are more sincere and more energetic in obedience than others; as though they exceeded the ordinary bounds in subduing and abasing themselves by obedience. (TA, from a trad.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
